question: Are the laws of the Old Testament still binding?
summary: Deuteronomy 7:9, 11:1, 12:1, and Psalm 119:151-160 declare the commandments and statutes binding 'forever,' 'always,' and 'to a thousand generations.' Jesus in Matthew 22:37-40 collapses the entire Law into two commandments. Luke 16:16 has Jesus say the Law and the prophets were only until John the Baptist. Either the Mosaic Law is permanently binding or it has been superseded.

reconcile.connective: Defenders answer that the Law was not abrogated but fulfilled — its force endures even as the new covenant brings it to its goal in Christ.

discrepancy.connective: Thomas Paine pressed the underlying objection: an immutable God cannot give one law in one age (the Old Testament) and a contrary law in another (the New), so the two-law scheme is self-refuting.

skeptic.name: Thomas Paine
skeptic.attribution: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason (1794)

pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, anticipating and rejecting the inference that 'the law and the prophets were until John' means the Law was 'abrogated and laid aside'; he argues it had 'their full accomplishment' in Christ. excerpts.excerpt_text: Although the new covenant fulfilled the Old Testament law and prophets, the law has not passed away …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers Luke 16:16's 'until John' horn and the abrogation claim: the Law is fulfilled, not superseded or void — the core harmonizing move for whether the Law is still binding.
excerpts.source_note_text: 16:17 that doesn’t mean that the law has lost its force: Although the new covenant fulfilled the Old Testament law and prophets, the law has not passed away (however, cp. Acts 15:23-29). • Heaven and earth will be destroyed and replaced by a new heaven and earth at the end of the age (Rev 21:1), but God’s word endures forever (Ps 119:89, 160; Isa 40:8; 55:10-11).
